subject: Life Skills
title: Tracking vs. Budgeting
description: A 60-second lesson on Tracking vs. Budgeting.

hook.text: She tracked every expense for a month using an app. The results shocked her: $300 on food delivery alone.

buildup.text: Tracking shows where money went. Budgeting decides where it will go. One is a mirror, the other is a map.

discovery.text: Most people skip tracking and jump to budgeting. But a budget based on guesses fails fast. Track first for one month.

twist.text: Tracking vs. Budgeting has a twist: the obvious interpretation usually breaks down.

climax.text: After one month of tracking, your real spending categories emerge. Build your budget from data, not from ideals.

punchline.text: Track before you budget. Reality beats guesswork.

quiz.question: Why should you track spending before creating a budget?
options: A budget built on actual data is more realistic than one built on guesses
You only need to track once in your life
